name: Canaan
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: Cursed be Canaan, a servant of servants unto his brethren.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

points: Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

points: The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia; Mizraim is Egypt; Phut is Libya, to the left of Egypt; and Canaan is the land where Jerusalem sits.
Ham inhabited what is known as Africa, and Canaan's land is the land of Israel; so the land of Israel is part of Africa.

note.label: Genesis 10: Shem, Ham, Japheth, and Nimrod

points: “And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.” Ham was the youngest son of Noah and one of the eight persons who lived through the flood. He became the progenitor of the dark races, but he is not the father of the Negroes: the Egyptians, Ethiopians, Libyans (not the modern ones you see today) and the Canaanites. The sons of Ham are the Hamites, the Nilotes. The Ishmaelites, the people of Ishmael, are the Arabs, a totally different race of people. The Arabs are not the ancient Egyptians nor Libyans, and the Caucasians are not the Jews, the children of Israel.

note.label: The Purpose of God's Wrath and Mercy

points: Put, and Canaan: there it is again. Put and Canaan.
The sons of Ham are named: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan, and the sons that came from them.
The line of Cush is traced through to Nimrod, and the sons of Mizraim and of Canaan are listed with the peoples that came from them.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 1: The Generations from Adam to Edom

points: And Canaan begat Zidon: remember that Canaan begat Zidon, because we're going to read some scriptures here and we're going to better understand who's who in the Bible. There is a difference, though.
And Canaan begat Zidon: Canaan begat who? Zidon. Canaan the son of Ham begat Zidon. So who dwelt in Tyre? The Zidonians, Hamites.
